title: Double-Take: Improving Capacity, Binding, and Selectivity In Long-Context Within Bidirectional Memory
abstract: arXiv:2610.13073v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Processing a long sequence does not guarantee that distant information remains usable. As context grows, a fixed-size memory must retain many associations, connect information across positions, and preserve relevant structure without being overwhelmed by everything it observes. These are distinct requirements: a memory may store more information without representing the relationships needed for retrieval, and it may transport those relationships without preserving the ones that matter. Thus, the challenge is not simply extending context length, but constructing a memory that remains usable as context grows. We study this problem in large-chunk test-time training (TTT) and identify two basic failures: single-step writes accumulate interference, limiting capacity, while self-associative writes cannot form cross-position bindings. We introduce Double-Take (DT), which repairs these failures with multi-step unpinned updates and cross-position

translated_title: Double-Take：在双向记忆中提升长上下文的容量、绑定与选择性
translated_abstract: 处理长序列并不能保证远处的信息依然可用。随着上下文的增长，固定大小的记忆必须保留大量关联、跨位置地连接信息，并保存相关的结构，而不被其所观察到的一切内容所淹没。这些是彼此不同的需求：记忆可能存储了更多信息，却没有表示出检索所需的关系；它也可能传递了这些关系，却没有保留其中重要的部分。因此，挑战不仅仅在于扩展上下文长度，而在于构建一个随着上下文增长仍保持可用的记忆。我们在大块测试时训练中研究这一问题，并识别出两种基本失败模式：单步写入会累积干扰，从而限制容量；而自关联写入无法形成跨位置的绑定。我们提出了 Double-Take (DT)，通过多步非固定更新与跨位置机制修复这些失败。（注：原文摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 提出 Double-Take 方法，通过多步非固定更新和跨位置机制，修复大块测试时训练中单步写入累积干扰限制容量、以及自关联写入无法形成跨位置绑定这两大基本失败，从而提升长上下文记忆的容量、绑定与选择性。
en_tdlr: Double-Take fixes two fundamental failures in large-chunk test-time training—interference accumulation from single-step writes and the inability of self-associative writes to form cross-position bindings—thereby improving capacity, binding, and selectivity in long-context memory.
